Supporting real hardware means more platform entries: more registry operations, more device paths, more firmware quirks. Each entry is trusted-by-declaration and enlarges the base a reader must audit. A kernel that boots on one QEMU machine type has an auditable trusted base; one that boots on real laptops does not.

